просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least, just', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'floor, storey' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас ведь второй этаж, да?
examples.trans: Ours is the second floor, right?
They live on the third floor.

examples.text: У нас ведь второй этаж, да? Давай, слушаем.
examples.trans: Ours is the second floor, right? Go on, let's listen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello, hi', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, I am really hungry for something.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('shared, common').

examples.trans: This is a shared bathroom, Vanya!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'well done; good person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мнить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to remember'.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'journalist, reporter' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are reporters out on the street!

examples.text: Там на улице журналисты! Они меня ждут!
examples.trans: There are reporters out on the street! They're waiting for me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'which, who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

examples.text: Который ему город подарил! И откуда у Аллы Евгеньевны новая шуба!
examples.trans: Which the city donated to him! And where Alla Yevgenyevna got a new fur coat!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on', paired with 'проследить'.

examples.trans: Keep an eye on the child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common Russian noun meaning 'kids; guys' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.
Then the boys will have a little word with you.
Right, kids, go out of the room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth; honestly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зникнуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arise, emerge', paired with 'возникать'.

examples.text: В ресторане опять возникли новые проблемы?
examples.trans: Have new problems arisen in the restaurant again?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'moron, idiot (colloq.)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you two total morons or what?

examples.text: Ты дебил, что ли, это удалить надо?
examples.trans: Are you an idiot or what, we have to delete this!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

нервничать.gloss: to be nervous, get worked up

meanings.en: to be nervous, get worked up
meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'рвничать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be nervous, get worked up'.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, вам нельзя нервничать сейчас.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, you mustn't get worked up right now.
I am not getting worked up!

examples.text: Я не нервничаю! Рейтинг Самсонова сравнялся с нашим?
examples.trans: I'm not getting worked up! Has Samsonov's rating drawn level with ours?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что? Ты мне ухо отрежешь?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what? Will you cut my ear off?

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'fool, idiot' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Костик, ты дурак! Это статусная вещь.
examples.trans: Kostik, you're a fool! This is a status piece.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, later, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
